functions: followLine (b4): one if / else if / else on the line tracker's reading, called again and again forever
control_flow: In followLine: if the line tracker reads below 30 %, curve left; else if it reads above 70 %, curve right; else drive straight at 20 %.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line from the start to the green goal at its end, through the curves, without leaving it.

decision_points.condition: first: the line tracker reads below 30 %; second: it reads above 70 %

branches.outcome: the floor under it is black (below 30 %): it curves left
the floor is bright, white band or peach (above 70 %): it curves right
the reading is in between (30 % to 70 %): it drives straight at 20 %

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left while the line tracker sees black, curves right while it sees white, and drives straight while the reading is in between
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on the black line, facing along it, with the green goal drawn over the line's end
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the white band, again and again, along the line and through its curves
scenarios.title: Follows the line to the goal at its end
assumptions: The green goal is at the end of the line.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line, through its curves, to the green goal at its end, without leaving the line

uncertainties: The middle part (a reading of 30 % to 70 %) happens only for a moment at the edge of the line's black core, where the program drives straight.
You don't say how tight the curves are: in a sharp bend a program that steers this way can lose the line.
On a plain floor the line tracker reads 83 %, so your program curves right and circles there: it needs the line under it.
